content.title: About
content.content: Processed cheese is a product made by melting natural cheese together with emulsifiers, salt, flavorings and sometimes added milk fats. It has a smooth, uniform texture, slices easily and melts quickly, making it popular in sandwiches, sauces and hot dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first industrial processed cheese was developed in Switzerland at the end of the 19th century.
Emulsifiers such as sodium phosphate salts keep the cheese homogeneous even at high temperatures.
Processed cheese is widely used in fast‑food because of its rapid meltability and long shelf life.
The product has different names worldwide: in the US – processed cheese, in Russia – плавленый сыр, in Japan – チーズスナック.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Delivers complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, supporting the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The smooth texture makes it gentle on the digestive system, especially for children and the elderly.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Offers quick energy through a combination of fats and carbohydrates.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Elevated salt levels can contribute to high blood pressure and fluid retention.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Contains saturated fatty acids, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or lactose may experience reactions.

items.title: Additives and preservatives
items.content: Often includes food additives that may be undesirable for those with sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Processed cheese is convenient sliced for sandwiches, grated into hot sauces, added to casseroles, omelets and pizza. It is also sold as meltable sticks and snack portions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. Shelf life is indicated on the label; after opening, use within 2–3 weeks. Discard if any mold, off‑odor, or discoloration appears.
